analysis.title: President Veto
key_insights: Associated Press is calling the Congressional race for the Democrats, who win the House and the Senate. The new Congress convenes at the start of 2027.
Trump retains veto and executive order powers, so the government is divided. Democrats will not have the two-thirds majority in both chambers needed to overturn a veto.
Rabobank's US strategist sees legislative gridlock as the more likely result, since the two parties share little common ground.

Gridlock should limit additional spending or tax cuts, but it also lowers the odds of a serious effort to shore up public finances. The term premium will probably keep US long-term rates pinned at higher levels.

A first government shutdown approaches on December 11, and the debt limit may bring more brinkmanship in 2027. The US economy should not expect a meaningful fiscal impulse, so the results could weigh on US equities.
With an unsupportive Congress, Trump will probably use executive orders to pursue foreign policy, trade policy and immigration, including the decision on whether to strike Iran again.

Oil futures fell sharply earlier in the week after Trump signalled he wants to give diplomacy another chance, and front-dated futures have stayed lower. The recent rise in 2027 pricing suggests markets are shifting toward tight supply and elevated transport costs into next year.
Rabobank remains sceptical that there is enough common ground for a US-Iran deal and believes escalation in the coming weeks is likelier than not.
By winning the Senate, Democrats can effectively block Trump's appointments, including potential replacements for Fed Governor Cook if she is forced out and for Powell if he resigns from the board.

Day ahead: the preliminary Eurozone October HICP is expected to show further impact of the energy shock, with headline consensus at 4.0% y/y and core steady at 2.5% y/y. Final PMIs for the Eurozone, UK and US are due, along with the US ISM services index.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Consensus expects headline inflation to accelerate on the energy shock. Member state estimates point to a similar print.
Core is seen steady, with no evidence so far that the energy shock is spreading.
Rabobank expects the term premium to keep US long-term rates pinned at higher levels given gridlock and weak odds of fiscal consolidation.

risk_factors: Legislative gridlock limits fiscal impulse and the odds of serious efforts to shore up public finances, which could weigh on US equities.
Government shutdown risk on December 11 and debt limit brinkmanship in 2027.
Escalation with Iran, with 2027 oil pricing rising on expected tight supply and elevated transport costs.
Possible Fed Governor changes (Cook, Powell) could be blocked by a Democratic Senate.
geopolitical: US midterm results give Democrats control of the House and Senate, while Trump keeps veto and executive order powers.
Trump is showing restraint on striking Iran again, saying he wants to give diplomacy another chance. Rabobank expects escalation in the coming weeks to be likelier than not.
A US government shutdown approaches on December 11, and the debt limit may cause more brinkmanship in 2027.
